data.description:
## Decision state

The operator deferred this decision on 2026-08-21. This ticket preserves the research and proposed design. It does not authorize an ADR or implementation.

## Current rebar mechanism

docs/README.md contains a generated-artifact table. tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py maintains separate GENERATED and GATED_HAND_AUTHORED collections and compares their projections with the table. A surface omitted from both collections remains undetected. The RP-05 ROUTES and CAPABILITIES registries do not contain generated ownership metadata.

## OSS research

Research used pinned default-branch revisions retrieved on 2026-08-21.

- CPython uses owner-local generator families plus an aggregate regen-all target. The aggregate explicitly excludes several manual regeneration targets. CI regenerates and checks Git status.
- Kubernetes combines centralized update commands, distributed source tags, filename-discovered verifiers, temporary-worktree regeneration, pre-generation cleanup, and an output manifest for generated documentation.
- Go uses distributed go:generate directives and generator-local output tables or parity tests. It has no repository-wide generated-output manifest.
- LLVM keeps build outputs in the CMake and TableGen dependency graph. Checked-in generated documents use separate owner-local scripts and byte comparisons.
- OpenAPI Generator uses declarative generation jobs and writes a FILES manifest for each generation output directory. CI regenerates and checks Git status.
- Rust uses typed owner-local bootstrap steps, shared output-path functions, and drift tests.

The comparison does not support a repository-wide record for every output. Such records would duplicate build graphs, declarative jobs, and generator-local path functions.

## Proposed design

Use one typed ownership descriptor beside each heterogeneous checked-in generator family. Each descriptor exposes the existing canonical sources, an output provider, generation entry point, verification entry point, marker policy, cleanup behavior, artifact lifecycle, and generated dependencies. The descriptor must call the same functions used by generation and verification instead of repeating their paths.

Maintain one explicit aggregate list of descriptors. The aggregate renders the contributor catalog, runs generation and drift checks, and validates duplicate ownership, output overlap, missing sources, empty dynamic sets, dependency cycles, stale outputs, and stray outputs. Avoid plugin discovery and source-text inference.

Use one descriptor per family rather than one record per output. Initial candidate families include CLI help, CLI reference, MCP reference, configuration and security reference, environment registry, ADR index, schema-derived types, plan criteria, prompt indexes, and synchronized templates.

Include checked-in generated files, generated sets, generated regions, synchronized copies, and parity mirrors. Exclude ephemeral build outputs whose build graph already owns dependencies and cleanup. Exclude authored demonstrations.

## Historical constraints

forworn-zanyish-narwhale introduced generated markers and the current contributor table after generated outputs were edited instead of their sources. ADR 0080 requires schema-derived contracts to retain one canonical schema authority. ADR 0100 rejects documentation-only grammars, source-text reconstruction, and additional parser authorities.

## Open questions

- Whether the descriptor protocol introduces an architectural invariant that warrants a new ADR.
- Which module should own the aggregate without making development metadata part of the public package surface.
- Whether aggregate verification should use a temporary worktree or a generated temporary directory.
- How synchronized regions should declare boundaries without duplicating their existing parity implementation.
- Which generated families need cleanup manifests for retired outputs.

## Resume condition

If the operator resumes this decision, complete a research critique before drafting any ADR. No implementation work begins until the decision completes its required lifecycle.
data.title: Decide generated-surface ownership descriptors
